name: scry
description: Session-start checks for project build state, running stack, repository health, concurrent activity, machine pressure, and untrusted Markdown. Requires every dispatch to a model to choose that model rather than inherit a default silently — subagents, workflow agents, and metered agent CLIs invoked through Bash — warns on first contact with a large and actively-worked source file, and guards expensive Elixir force-rebuilds. Tells a spawned subagent when the worktree it was handed is behind origin/main, notes when a session writes Markdown this repo's conventions do not expect. A PreToolUse ADVISORY speaks when a Bash command creates a branch without naming a start point, giving how far HEAD sits behind origin/<default> and how old the last fetch is, since a count measured against a stale remote-tracking ref is itself stale; SCRY_BRANCH_POINT_FETCH_HOURS (default 2) sets when a fetch counts as dated. It never fetches, moves nothing, and denies nothing. A plugin monitor (Claude only) watches when the session's prompt cache goes cold — read from the status-line payload, the only place Claude Code reports it, via a small wrapper the user points statusLine at once — and, at most once per user message, asks the session to write a summary as its reply in the conversation while the cache is still warm — never to a file — opening with the full session id and how to pick it up in a new window; a UserPromptSubmit hook is what re-arms it, and only for a user message, so tool calls, cache hits, task and monitor notifications, and the summary itself never do. It follows the session a /clear starts in the same process. While work the session started is unfinished, it sends instead a keep-alive with a roster of that work as Scry can read it from metadata (workflows with an agent started and no result, however quiet; background commands whose output file a process still holds open; subagents written within SCRY_KEEPALIVE_FRESH_SECS, default 3600, with what the silence means once it nears the TTL) and asks for one status line for the user, compared with the previous one, checking on any worker that has not moved — Scry reports, the session judges. At most SCRY_KEEPALIVE_MAX (default 8) times per user message, then it asks for the summary with the unfinished work named. SCRY_CACHE_HANDOFF=0 disables it; SCRY_CACHE_HANDOFF_LEAD_SECONDS (default 120) sets how long before expiry it speaks. statusline.sh is a whole status line for Claude Code (Claude only): folder, branch when off the default, uncommitted and unpushed counts when non-zero, model, session cost, other live sessions in the directory, the seven-day window with its reset day, context as tokens over the window, and the cache segment — minutes until it goes cold, and the size of the re-read the next request pays once it has. A SessionEnd hook records which session a /clear ended (id, transcript path, directory, time; one small file under $TMPDIR, deleted when the next session reads it, swept after a day), so the session that replaces it is told exactly which one it left, its transcript path, what resuming it costs, and whether Scry asked it for a summary before it went idle — read from Scry's own state file, so the successor knows whether the end of that transcript holds one. It also names what that session left RUNNING: the subagents still writing under its session id, and the background jobs under it that recorded no result. A subagent, workflow agent or background job outlives the session that launched it, but its result reports to a session id that takes no more turns — and before 1.29.0 this hook filed those subagents under "other sessions", which reads as somebody else's work and is what makes a replacement session start the same build a second time on the same branch. At SessionStart it flags open PRs that passed review and CI but sit unqueued, PRs knocked out of the merge queue, checks that failed after passing on the run before, and an idle merge queue while reviewed PRs wait. At SessionStart it also names subfolders below the start folder that carry their own AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md and that what they say is not in context during early planning, search, naming, and builder briefs; and at SessionStart and after a write of an AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, it names any folder whose AGENTS.md has no CLAUDE.md that links to or imports it.

interface.shortDescription: See repository and machine state at session start
interface.longDescription: Adds session-start context about project build state, the stack the system actually runs on, repository hygiene, concurrent Claude and Codex activity, local machine pressure, and why every repository Markdown file is untrusted historical material. Also installs one PreToolUse hook that DENIES a first attempt at an artifact-discarding Elixir rebuild (`mix compile --force`, `rm -rf _build`) and states its cost; running the command again within five minutes passes through untouched. Set SCRY_BUILD_GUARD=0 to disable that hook. A second PreToolUse hook DENIES any dispatch that names no model, because a blank model is not a default -- it silently inherits whatever default is already in place, for the whole run, multiplied across a fan-out. That covers Agent and Workflow dispatch, and metered agent CLIs run through Bash, where an unflagged call falls back to the CLI's own config default; SCRY_METERED_CLIS (default codex) sets which CLIs are covered and SCRY_METERED_CLI_GUARD=0 switches that part off. No model is forbidden; only the absent choice is. On the same surface, a headless `claude -p` run while ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set is refused ONCE with what it will bill -- that run is metered against the API account rather than the subscription -- and the same command repeated within five minutes proceeds; SCRY_API_BILLING_GUARD=0 silences it. A PostToolUse note reports what a premium model draws after it is deliberately chosen, and SCRY_PREMIUM_MODELS sets which models draw it. A further PostToolUse advisory speaks on first contact with a source file that is both large and actively worked, naming what it did not return and what goes wrong silently at that size. Two further ADVISORY hooks inject context and never deny anything. A SubagentStart hook tells a spawned subagent that the worktree it was handed is behind origin/main, by how many commits and days, and how to read the live tip instead -- SessionStart context does not reach a subagent, so an agent otherwise searches a stale tree and reports a feature missing when it merely is not checked out; it fires only when that worktree is on the default branch, it never fetches, and it never moves a ref or a file.
